I will keep my land in the usual North China Plain rotation: winter wheat followed by summer maize. In Quzhou County, that is still the most reliable way for me to use the full year, match the local climate, and spread my risk across two main grain crops. Because I am educated and want stable output, I will use improved or hybrid seed instead of saving weak seed. I will keep fertilizer rates moderate rather than excessive, because I want yield, but I also know too much nitrogen wastes money and can increase lodging and disease pressure. I will irrigate wheat more often than maize, since wheat here depends heavily on timely water at jointing and grain filling, while maize can usually get by with fewer irrigations if summer rain is normal. I will use rotary tillage for wheat establishment after maize harvest because it is efficient on my scale, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize into wheat stubble to save time and conserve moisture during the tight harvest-planting window. I will not spray blindly; I will keep a limited number of pesticide applications aimed at the main local weeds, aphids, rusts, armyworm, and corn borer when needed. My goal is steady grain yield, manageable costs, and low disruption during the busy season.
